notes_for_editor.note: No source found on staffing history, decommission date, restoration, or current public access/climbability for Parker Springs specifically. The built year (1937) comes from a single hobbyist survey site (Jackson's Ramblings), not an NRHP nomination or Forest Service document; treat it as plausible but not strongly corroborated. height_m (30.5) is a conversion of the 100-ft tower height stated by NHLR, not independently confirmed.

No source documents staffing history, when fire-watch use ended, or whether the 2013-2016 restoration talk ever resulted in the tower being opened to climbers; current access/climbable status should be verified before publishing a stronger claim. The eastern_us_lookouts cache page (easternuslookouts.weebly.com/wharton.html) was checked but contains only the tower name, county, and preserve name with no additional prose, so it was not cited.

The NHLR narrative text says NRHP acceptance was 'October, 1995' while the official NRHP reference number's listing date (via Wikipedia/NRIS) is September 11, 1995; I used the official date and noted the discrepancy. Access status recorded as 'unknown' in facts because sources describe a locked gate on the road but say nothing about whether climbing the tower itself is permitted; did not mark it climbable. Did not use any WebSearch calls; three cached/live page reads (NHLR, Central US Lookouts, Wikipedia) were sufficient. Fact-check (2026-10-04): the summit elevation is also given inconsistently across sources -- NHLR says 1,089 ft, Wikipedia says 1,150 ft; the story follows NHLR since that is the only source the elevation sentence cites, but a human may want to reconcile the two.

The FS trail page lists the trail under the Payson Ranger District; the NHLR page (and the record) say Pleasant Valley Ranger District. Both are districts of Tonto National Forest; this may reflect a later district reorganization rather than a factual error, but I did not resolve it and left the record's district attribution untouched. Height (~41 ft) and the 'closed to motorized travel' wilderness note come from Mountain Field Guide, a secondary aggregator that cites the Forest Service and Peakbagger; treat with slightly less confidence than the NHLR and USFS primary sources. Climbability of the tower itself (public access to the cab) is not established by any source read; left as unknown.

Current operational status is genuinely disputed between sources: NHLR (page last updated 2016) describes the tower as in active service, and Wikipedia separately attributes a 'open to visitors when staffed in summer' description to the Forest Service -- but checked directly, the USFS Kendrick Mountain Trail #22 page itself says nothing about staffing or visitor access, so that claim should not be cited to the trail page. Wikipedia also says the tower looked damaged and likely abandoned as of mid-2024, with no cited source for that claim. Worth a human check (e.g. a recent trip report or current USFS fire lookout roster) before updating the tower's staffing/access fields. The tower record's 'kind' field (two_story) comes from FFLA's '2-Story Cab' classification, which doesn't obviously match NHLR's description of a flat-roof cab on a 10 ft tower -- plausibly just differing naming conventions rather than a real conflict, so no correction proposed, but flagging it.

Good primary-register coverage (NHLR + NRHP nomination metadata + FFLA list), but nothing on named lookouts, specific fires, visitor access, or current staffing/climbability turned up in cache or the three web searches used. The elevation figure conflicts between NHLR (8,467 ft) and the NRHP record (8,250 ft) and should be looked at by someone who can check the actual nomination PDF or a topo map. Height is also given two ways (48 ft vs 49 ft) by the two registers. No cached page existed for this specific lookout outside nhlr/ and ffla/; fflos (abandoned-sites register) has no AZ Lake Mountain entry, consistent with it still standing and in service.

Current staffing/access status is only as current as these pages (dates on them unclear), so the tower record's staffing/access fields are left 'unknown' rather than overwritten; story says staffed 'each fire season' per source wording. No photos beyond the one already in the tower record were found within budget.

The 1916-1923 staffing/construction detail comes from an enthusiast compilation site (californialookouts.weebly.com) that cites period Siskiyou County newspapers and a 1952 USC&GS data sheet; I could not verify those primary sources directly, only the compiler's summary of them, so treat names/dates in events for 1916-1923 as secondhand. The NHLR-dated 1938 tower and the 1919 lookout house are almost certainly two different structures on the same peak (record's 'built: 1938' event refers only to the surviving tower) - worth a note on the tower page if the editor wants to preserve both construction dates. Several undated NHLR photos (a 'California Plan 4A Cabin' and a 'Tree Platform') suggest yet other structures/eras on this site that no source dates; not added as events since no year is given. Kathy Shoopman's start-year lookout is called 'Bald Mountain Lookout' in the Action News Now piece but multiple other outlets (ABC10, Yahoo/AP, KTVL) place her first post at 'Baldy Mountain Lookout... west of Happy Camp', matching this record; I treated it as the same site given the matching location description, but flagging the name discrepancy. No source found addresses current public access, trail, or drive-up status, so visit/access facts were left out rather than guessed.

Record's 'design' and 'height_m' fields are still null; NHLR only confirms it is an enclosed tower cab (matched by FFLA's 'Encl. Tower'), not a specific design code (e.g. L-4) or structure height. Current access level for visitors (open vs restricted) isn't stated by either source beyond the gated BLM road detail, so access.level is left unknown rather than guessed. Fact-check 2026-10-04: the original draft claimed Cahto Peak's own FFLOS registry number was 'US 2049, CA 155' — on the FFLOS list that number actually belongs to the adjacent, unrelated, 'Gone' listing for Cahoon Rock; Cahto Peak's own FFLOS row instead cross-references the NHLR number (US 1125, CA 110). Story and this evidence entry were corrected to drop the misattributed FFLOS number.

Two distinct prior structures are easy to conflate: (1) a 1924 lookout on Bear Basin Butte itself, burned 1936, unrelated to the current building; (2) the Camp Six/Upper Coon Mountain cabin (built 1934 per NHLR, or first built 1923 per FFLOS with an undated later replacement cabin) that was moved to Bear Basin Butte in 1996 (recreation.gov) or 1997 (FFLOS) and is the structure standing today. The tower record's own 'built: 1934' event matches NHLR but not FFLOS; left as-is since it's directly sourced. No corrections proposed to the tower record itself -- its fields (name, location, status 'relocated', agency) all check out against these sources. The FFLA CA list entry confirms 'Relocated' status and the NHLR US 288/CA 21 numbers; an adjacent table row for a different lookout (Basalt Hill, NHLR US 880/CA 90) sits right next to this one in the cached HTML and could be misread as a conflicting register number for Bear Basin Butte -- it is not, it belongs to the preceding row.

Design history (three successive structures, 1925/1931/1961) is well documented by NHLR, but no source gives named keepers, specific fires spotted, or a current staffing/access status beyond NHLR's general 'staffed daily during fire season' line, which is undated and may be stale. NHLR's descriptive paragraph also mentions 'Mi-Wok Ranger District, 4,939' elevation' separately from the page's stated lookout elevation of 4,931 ft; this reads like boilerplate district text rather than a conflicting lookout elevation, so no correction is proposed.

No independent source beyond NHLR and the FFLA Colorado list was found in the cache or a quick check; both agree on name, location and standing status (FFLA uses 'Deadman Mountain'). The NHLR page is unusually detailed for a short tower (CCC predecessor, 2004 visit narrative, 2019 condition note, Sprint cell-site encroachment), so confidence is medium rather than low despite having only one substantive source. Worth flagging: do not confuse with the unrelated 'Deadman Mountain Lookout' in Wyoming, which also appears in the raw cache and is a different structure.

Coordinates (38.040996, -105.012697, elev ~2252m per OSM) fall in the Wet Mountains near Greenhorn Mountain/St Charles Peak/Lake Isabel, San Isabel National Forest area, but no cached or web source ties a named lookout to that exact point. Checked every cached NHLR and FFLOS Colorado entry's coordinates (both index pages) and none are within a reasonable distance of this node. Three WebSearch queries (generic coordinate/region search, San Isabel NF fire tower history, named Wet Mountains peaks) turned up nothing specific to this structure. Possible the OSM 'Fire Tower' label is generic (e.g. a different kind of tower, or a genuinely obscure/undocumented lookout) rather than a proper name — worth a human look if better aerial/historic-map sources become available.

Exact height_m and precise CCC construction dates beyond 1940 were not found; RIDB only says 'built in the 1940s' while NHLR gives 1940 specifically, so I used 1940. No conflicting built-year sources requiring a resolved_conflicts entry. Status/climbability for independent day hikers beyond the paid overnight rental is not documented in the sources read; left visit.climbable unset rather than guess.

Build year conflict: NHLR says 1931, two other sources say 1934; went with the majority. Last staffed year given as 1969 by two sources, consistent. 'Known staff' date of 1967 (Thomas Langseth) predates the stated last-staffed year of 1969, which is plausible but not reconciled further. Spot check against idahofirelookouts.com found the story's original 'steam locomotives' detail was not supported by the source (which only says 'Milwaukee Railroad', and the line through this stretch was historically electrified, not steam) and the Loop Creek sentence copied the source's phrasing too closely; both were fixed in the story.

Build-year conflict between NHLR (1960, with full structure history) and Recreation.gov (1956) is unresolved; NHLR's account is more detailed so it was treated as primary. Full staffing history beyond the single 1967 relief lookout was not found within the search budget.

Build year (1937 vs 1938) and tower height (72 ft vs 84 ft) conflict between NHLR and the other two sources; noted in the story rather than resolved. NHLR's own record page says the tower is 'available for rental,' which conflicts a little with the record's access.level of 'unknown' -- worth a look, but I left access as unknown in facts since no source confirms public climbing access, only rental/standby status.

The tower record's 'rental' block and the 'Lookout Butte Lookout' alias both appear to actually describe a different, separately registered lookout (NHLR US 769) about 40 miles northeast of Black Butte on the same forest -- see the two proposed corrections. If that's confirmed, Lookout Butte Lookout likely needs (or already has) its own record with that rental data. Core build-history facts about Black Butte itself (1925 camp, 1928 cupola cabin, 1970 Region 6 Flat Top rebuild) are corroborated by two independent sources (NHLR and firelookout.com) and match in every detail, so confidence in those is good. However, current status is genuinely disputed: NHLR and FFLA (firelookout.org) list it as standing, while a separate, uncached Idaho Fire Lookouts page for this exact lookout (same coordinates/elevation/build history, in their Selway-region listing, source 6) marks it 'Abandoned' with no further detail. The original research checked only idahofirelookouts.com's West Central region page (source 5, which covers an unrelated same-named lookout) and missed this direct conflict. Confidence is capped at medium because of this unresolved status conflict and because the access/rental story still needs a human to verify and fix in the live record.

The tower record's 'conflicts' entry lists firelookout_com as giving a built year of 1928, but that page's actual text matches nhlr exactly (1916/1928/1950 sequence) — likely a mis-extraction when the record was built. Recommend the conflict be cleared rather than left open; no new correction filed since the record's 'built: 1950' field is already right. Fact-check 2026-10-04: removed a sentence claiming secondary listings 'collapse' the three build dates and citing recreation.gov for the full 1916/1928/1950 sequence — no evidence quote supported that framing (recreation.gov's page does independently state the same three dates, confirmed by spot-check, but the sentence as written made an unsupported claim about other listings). Also rewrote the 1950-cab sentence, which copied the nhlr.org description almost verbatim.
Build-year conflict (1934 vs 1936) left unresolved per two-against-one source split. No structure height (as opposed to elevation) was found in sources, so height_m was omitted.

Idaho Fire Lookouts lists many more named seasonal staff (Odell, Black, Walters, Baker, Voll, etc.) between 1946 and 1972; only a sample is named in the story to keep it readable, with full list available in the source. Cabin footprint (15x15 vs 14x14) differs slightly between NHLR and Recreation.gov; both are given rather than resolved.

Minor year conflict (1956 vs 1957) for the current cabin's construction, noted in the story and resolved_conflicts. Two small date conflicts in the sources, both noted in the story rather than resolved: last staffed year (NHLR: 1968; Deseret News: 1969) and the restoration year before the 2008 closure (NHLR: 1986; Deseret News: early-1980s renovation, reopened 1987). Fact-check pass (2026-10-04) found the original story had miscited and conflated two of its numbers. The rebuilder's page gives no height at all for the original Fort Lewis tower, and separately dates its construction to 1966, not 1968 (a discrepancy the original story missed entirely). A travel-blog page (roadtripryan.com) and the WebSearch AI summary both offered a vivid, specific narrative - an 1922 primitive fire watch predecessor and a 1938 lightning strike that set the lookout's bed on fire - that appears nowhere in the NHLR register, the FFLA register, or the Forest Service's own Bighorn lookouts history page. A footnote error was also fixed: the story had attributed the 'Emergency' staffing status to 'the Forest Fire Lookout Association's own register,' but that fact actually comes from firelookout.com, an independent reference site by Rex Kamstra, not from FFLA's own site (firelookout.org, source 3) - the FFLA page for Wyoming is just a name/county/status table with no staffing field for this lookout. research_corrections.name: Hager Mountain Lookout

research_corrections.name: Clearwater Lookout
research_corrections.current: 1938 (per NHLR 'Built' field, used in the tower record)
research_corrections.proposed: 1933 for the steel tower; 1935 for the ground cabin

research_corrections.name: Evergreen Mountain Lookout
research_corrections.current: Rental description (sourced from Recreation.gov/ridb) states the lookout was placed on the NRHP during 1990s volunteer restoration; willhiteweb.com independently repeats the same claim.
research_corrections.proposed: NPGallery's own NRHP asset record gives a listing date of July 14, 1987, a decade before the restoration effort described on Recreation.gov and willhiteweb.com. The two popular accounts agree with each other but disagree with the primary NRHP record; this should be reconciled or flagged in the record.
research_corrections.evidence: NPGallery AssetDetail page for NRIS 87001187 states a listing date of July 14, 1987 as part of a multiple-property submission; Recreation.gov's description ('During volunteer restoration efforts in the 1990s, the lookout was placed on the National Register of Historic Places') and willhiteweb.com ('During restoration it was placed on the National Register of Historic Places') both attribute the listing to the 1990s restoration instead.
